title: Bridging the Evaluation Gap: Leveraging Large Language Models for Topic Model Evaluation
venue: 21st Conference on Information and Research Science Connecting to Digital and Library Science (IRCDL 2025); arXiv 2502.07352
task: Multi-dimensional automatic evaluation of topic models with open LLMs
problem: Human evaluation is costly and statistical metrics are narrow; evolving topic taxonomies in digital libraries need scalable evaluation.
architecture: Prompted LLM metrics for coherence (rating C_rate, outlier detection C_outlier), repetitiveness (R_rate, duplicate concepts R_duplicate), diversity (D_rate) and topic-document alignment (irrelevant topic words, missing themes); adversarial tests to check evaluator reliability; three open LLM judges.

datasets.name: 20NG
datasets.details: OCTIS version, 11,415 train and 4,894 test documents

datasets.name: AGRIS
datasets.details: 50,067 agricultural scholarly documents (45,060 train / 5,007 test), split into sentences

key_results: Adversarial outlier detection success: 77% (Mistral), 81% (Llama), 90% (Qwen) on 20NG; duplicate detection only 37% for Mistral vs 84% for Qwen.
BERTopic has the best Cv and LLM coherence rating (e.g. AGRIS K = 50: Cv 0.655, Qwen C_rate 2.878) but low repetitiveness scores, suggesting redundant top words inflate its coherence.
strengths: Adds repetitiveness and topic-document alignment dimensions missing from Cv/TD.
Uses open models and tests evaluator reliability explicitly.

limitations.text: LLM evaluators disagree substantially (e.g. on outliers for BERTopic at K = 100), so several judges are needed.
No human annotation to validate the LLM metrics directly.
